fact_notes: Growth rate: fingernails grow about 3 to 3.47 mm per month, toenails about 1.5 to 1.62 mm per month. Cleveland Clinic nail anatomy page; 2010 study reported by Verywell Health.

Stone Age: NO direct evidence survives - no fingernails survive from Stone Age burials, so wear, biting, flint edges and rough-stone filing are inference from daily labour and tool use. The film says this on screen (line 7).

Babylon: royal tombs in Ur, southern Babylon, yielded a multi-piece manicure set with solid gold implements; Babylonian noblemen manicured with solid gold tools, traced to about 3200 BC. NAILS Magazine history; nail-care textbook summaries.

Egypt: manicure instruments found in royal tombs; Egyptians trimmed/shaped with copper and bronze tools, buffed with pumice, stained with henna, red marking highest status. NAILS Magazine; NailPeak ancient nails guide.
Written mention: descriptions of nail trimming date to the 8th century BC; Deuteronomy 21:12 - she shall shave her head and trim her nails. Wikipedia Nail clipper; Atlas Obscura 2017.
Paring: before the modern clipper, people used small knives to trim or pare their nails. Wikipedia Nail clipper history.
Rome: Horace, Epistles (about 20 BC): a close-shaven man in an empty barber booth, penknife in hand, quietly cleaning his nails. Atlas Obscura; National Geographic 2024.

Roman toilet sets: bronze implements strung like a ring of keys - tweezers, ear scoop, dedicated nail cleaner; V-shaped type in Roman Britain could also serve as a file. National Geographic 2024; ScienceABC.

Medieval: small shears resembling yarn cutters, or small ordinary blades; small sharp knife and pumice as file. SwissKlip history; Calendar-Australia FAQ. Weakest-sourced era - narration stays generic.

China: long fingernails a status symbol in Qing dynasty (1644-1912) Manchu high culture, showing no manual labour; protectors of gold, silver, jade, tortoiseshell; Cixi portraits show nails exceeding three inches. Pitt Rivers Museum Body Arts. Origin earlier (Warring States) but film places era at Qing peak so time only moves forward.

Clipper patents: first US patent for an improvement in finger-nail clippers filed 1875 by Valentine Fogerty (US 161112); clamp-style recognisable today patented 1881 by Eugene Heim and Celestin Matz. Wikipedia; Atlas Obscura 2017. Fogerty 1875 device was closer to a circular file - film wording reflects arrival, not finished design.
Modern: mass-produced stainless lever clippers are the present-day default - general knowledge, no specific claim.
